nodes.name: PdCuNiCoZn high-entropy metallene synthesis
nodes.procedure: First, 10 mg of Pd(acac)₂, 10 mg of Co(acac)₂, 8 mg of Ni(acac)₂, 10 mg of Cu(acac)₂, 6 mg of Zn(acac)₂, 80 mg of ascorbic acid and 60 mg of W(CO)₆ were dissolved in 16 mL of DMF and 4 mL of acetic acid, followed by ultrasonication for 1 h. Second, the transparent solution was sealed in a glass bottle and transferred to an oil bath at 90 °C for 12 h. After it was naturally cooled to room temperature, the colloidal product was washed with a mixture of ethanol and cyclohexane six times and then dried at 60 °C for future use.

nodes.name: PdCuNiCo quaternary metallene synthesis
nodes.procedure: First, 10 mg of Pd(acac)₂, 10 mg of Co(acac)₂, 8 mg of Ni(acac)₂, 10 mg of Cu(acac)₂, 60 mg of ascorbic acid and 60 mg of W(CO)₆ were dissolved in 16 ml of DMF and 4 mL of acetic acid, followed by ultrasonication for 1 h. nodes.name: PdCuNi ternary metallene synthesis
nodes.procedure: First, 10 mg of Pd(acac)₂, 10 mg of Co(acac)₂, 8 mg of Ni(acac)₂, 40 mg of ascorbic acid, and 60 mg of W(CO)₆ were dissolved in 16 mL of DMF and 4 mL of acetic acid, followed by ultrasonication for 1 h. Second, the transparent solution was sealed in a glass bottle and transferred to an oil bath at 80 °C for 12 h. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the colloidal product was washed with a mixture of ethanol and cyclohexane several times and then dried at 60 °C for future use.

nodes.name: PdCu bimetallene synthesis
nodes.procedure: First, 12 mg of Pd(acac)₂, 8 mg of Cu(acac)₂, and 40 mg of W(CO)₆ were dispersed in 16 mL of DMF and 4 mL of acetic acid, followed by ultrasonication for 15 min and then heating to 70 °C for 2 h. The black colloidal product was washed with ethanol six times and dried at 60 °C for future use.

nodes.description: NO3RR performance in neutral electrolyte (0.1 M KNO3 + 0.5 M K2SO4, pH = 7 ± 0.3)
nodes.source_text: amperometric i-t measurements were conducted in 0.1 M KNO3/0.5 M K2SO4 to quantitatively evaluate the NO3RR activity... The highest NH3 yield rate was observed at -1.2 V versus RHE, which exceeded 275 mg h⁻¹ mg⁻¹, and a maximum NH3 Faradaic efficiency of 95.4% was achieved at -0.6 V versus RHE. Notably, PdCuNiCoZn high-entropy metallenes also show high Faradaic efficiency (>90%) over a wide operating potential window from -0.6 V to -1.0 V versus RHE

nodes.description: NO3RR performance in strongly alkaline electrolyte (0.1 M KNO3 + 1.0 M KOH, pH = 14 ± 0.2)
nodes.source_text: the NO3RR activity of PdCuNiCoZn was further investigated in a strongly alkaline electrolyte (0.1 M KNO3/1.0 M KOH, pH = 14 ± 0.2)... The NH3 Faradic efficiency exhibited a typical volcano trend, and a maximum NH3 Faradaic efficiency greater than 99.0% was achieved at -0.5 V versus RHE. The highest NH3 yield rate is observed at -0.8 V versus RHE, which is greater than 447 mg h⁻¹ mg⁻¹

nodes.description: Long-term stability test in neutral electrolyte at -0.9 V vs RHE

stability.value: morphology, crystal structure, and chemical state remained almost unchanged

nodes.source_text: During the cycling stability test at -0.9 V versus RHE in 0.5 M K2SO4/0.1 M KNO3, the NH3 yield rate remained above 120 mg h⁻¹ mg⁻¹ and the Faradaic efficiency remained above 85% after 50 h of running. According to the characterization via TEM, XRD, and XPS, the morphology, crystal structure, and chemical state of the high-entropy metallene remained almost unchanged after electrolysis

nodes.source_text: linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) was performed in 0.5 M K2SO4 with different concentrations of NO3- (Fig. 3a). nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows typical graphene-like structure of PdCuNiCoZn high-entropy metallene.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A PdCuNiCoZn high-entropy metallene was obtained, which exhibited a typical graphene-like structure, as shown by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) images (Fig. 1a, b)

nodes.evidence_snippet: with a thickness of 1.98 nm, as measured via atomic force microscopy (AFM) (Supplementary Fig. 1)

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping and line scanning confirm uniform distributions of Pd, Cu, Ni, Co, and Zn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) line scanning confirmed the uniform distributions of Pd, Cu, Ni, Co, and Zn (Supplementary Fig. 2)

The atomic ratio of each element in the PdCuNiCoZn high-entropy metallene was further determined to be Pd/Co/Ni/Cu/Zn = 23.9/24.7/20.1/24.3/7.0 via inductively coupled plasma‒optical emission spectrometry (ICP‒OES)

nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image revealed that the interplanar spacing of 0.215 nm could be attributed to the (111) plane of the face-centred cubic (fcc) structure (Fig. 1c)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peak at ~41° for (111) plane of fcc lattice with positive shift and lower intensity indicating lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Upon further characterization of the crystal structure via X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Fig. 1d), the diffraction peak at approximately 41° could be attributed to the (111) plane of the fcc lattice

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM shows high density of single atoms anchored in crystalline region with fcc structure confirmed by FFT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) images of the high-entropy metallene from the randomly selected crystalline regions are provided (Fig. 1e and f, Supplementary Fig. 19)

nodes.characterization_summary: XAS including XANES shows Pd K-edge similar to Pd foil indicating metallic Pd dominant; Cu, Ni, Co, Zn K-edges shifted positively confirming positive valence states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: synchrotron radiation X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) characterization, including X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectroscopy, was performed. The K-edge adsorption energy of Pd is similar to that of Pd foil (Fig. 2a), indicating that metallic Pd is dominant

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Pd-Cu at 2.46 Å, Pd-Ni, Pd-Co, Pd-Zn bonds with no M-M peaks confirming atomic dispersion of Cu, Ni, Co, Zn single atoms on Pd-based metallene.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS spectra (R space) after Fourier transformations of the original data are shown in Fig. 2f-j. For the EXAFS spectra of Cu, the peak at 2.46 Å could be assigned to the Pd‒Cu bond... no Cu‒Cu coordination peaks belonging to Cu or CuO are detected, further confirming the atomic dispersion of Cu
